items.description:
Eden Beauty Collection is a hair and beauty salon at 6A Kromboom Road in Rondebosch, Cape Town. Its services include hair styling, hair extensions, laser hair removal, manicures and pedicures, gel nails, waxing and threading. Lash services cover classic, hybrid and volume lashes, along with lamination and lift treatments.

The salon has a 4.9 rating from more than 1,700 reviews on its Fresha booking page, and its team has more than eight practitioners. The Fresha listing also shows package deals and promotions. Clients can book online, and the salon suits people in Rondebosch who want hair, nails, lashes and laser treatments in an upmarket but relaxed setting.

The salon uses Davines hair products, and it offers manicures and pedicures with OPI and Essie polishes. Clients can book through its Fresha listing, which shows the salon's address and services. Its Fresha profile lists hair services alongside nail treatments, so clients can book several services at once. It suits clients in Lakeside and nearby suburbs who want hair and nail work in one place.

The company describes its range as the widest in South Africa, and it offers a fully installed flooring service for homes and businesses. Customers can visit the showroom or call the branch, and the contact page lists its opening hours for each day of the week. The showroom suits homeowners, builders and businesses in Paarden Eiland and the surrounding northern suburbs who need flooring supplied and fitted.

Hair Ambitions is a hair salon in Plattekloof Village on Plattekloof Road, Cape Town. It was formerly known as Eclipse Styling Studio and was bought over at the beginning of 2011. The salon offers colour, highlights, cutting, styling, Brazilian blow dries, hair extensions and a nail bar.

The salon is Goldwell-affiliated and uses KMS and Joico products. Its village listing describes it as one of the trendier salons in the area and says it strives for service excellence. Its village location sits alongside convenience shops such as Pick n Pay and Woolworths. It suits clients in Plattekloof and nearby suburbs who want colour, styling and nail services in one visit.

The International School of Cape Town is a Cambridge school in Bishopscourt, Cape Town, teaching from Nursery through to High School and A Levels. The school describes itself as one of the oldest Cambridge schools in the country, offering the Cambridge curriculum since 1998.

The school says it combines excellent academic results with a warm and supportive environment, and it uses the latest in teaching methods and technology. Cambridge qualifications are accepted by more than 1,400 universities, and students can transfer between more than 10,000 Cambridge schools in over 160 countries. It suits families who want an internationally recognised curriculum for their children.

Kraaifontein Hardware is a family-run hardware store in Belmont Park, Kraaifontein, established in 1975. Its range covers building materials, sand and gravel, bricks, cement and cement blocks, steel reinforcing and steel-cutting equipment, timber, and wood-cutting equipment.

The store also stocks plumbing equipment, tools, drilling and abrasive equipment, nuts and bolts, screws, keys and electrical supplies, along with paint and housewares. Its website describes the business as having passion and care for hardware. The store has traded in Belmont Park since it was established in 1975. It suits builders, tradespeople and homeowners in Kraaifontein who need materials and tools from one local store.

Leopards Panel Beaters is an auto body repair shop in Epping, Cape Town. It offers panel beating, accident repair, spray painting, dent repair, buff and polish, rust removal, scratch removal and leak detection.

The business presents itself as a trusted panel beater in Cape Town, and it says it combines affordable prices with quality work. Its site lists its services and an about section for customers who want to know more. Accident repair is handled alongside cosmetic work such as scratch and dent removal, so one shop covers most body damage. It suits vehicle owners in Epping and the surrounding northern suburbs who need bodywork, paint or minor damage repaired.

Marine Solutions is a Cape Town company founded in 1999 to support the offshore industry in Southern Africa, and it now works more widely. Its main areas are ROV sales, ROV equipment support and pilot and technical training, along with cable assembly, manufacturing and overmoulding.

The company says its strength is the practical and technical knowledge its team has gained across different engineering fields. It recently achieved an ISO certification covering quality, environment and safety. Its work spans sales, support, training and cable assembly, so clients can use one supplier for equipment and trained staff. It suits offshore and subsea clients who need ROV equipment, support or trained pilots.

Out of Africa is an African gifts and souvenirs store on the Upper Level of Victoria Wharf at the V&A Waterfront. It sells authentic African gifts, crafts and curios, including handcrafted ceramics, basketry, home decor and jewellery.

The store's listing features local makers, and the products are sourced through community upliftment programmes, according to the store. The Waterfront listing gives a rating of 3.7 from 32 Google reviews. Its gifts range from small curios to home decor. It suits visitors who want to take home a gift or souvenir from Cape Town, and shoppers looking for handcrafted African products.
